The entire staged section is correct under the four supplied, independently audited internal premises. The 1/n normalization is exact. Monotone trace control gives a finite positive matrix sum almost everywhere, integrable coefficients, and the exact tail norm ||S-S_N||=2^{-N}M. Distributional uniqueness identifies this sum with the full current omega+ddc U and yields the stated approximation bound 2^{1-N}M.

For every finite N, delta_N omega>0 permits bounded residual truncation. The inequality V_N>=U on {U>-t} is correct. Bounded plurifine locality identifies the restricted truncation measures, and positive mixed products dominate S_N^n. Exhaustion outside the volume-null pole set and determinant monotone convergence establish domination on every Borel set, allowing infinite measures. The lower bound 2^j for every N>=j proves infinite pointwise determinant integral and divergence of the full sequence of smooth masses. Extended mass is consequently infinite.

The corollary correctly gives the strict lower bound (1-epsilon)omega, both L1 convergences, the full-trace total-variation bound epsilon||T-omega||, trivial multiplier ideals for every p>0, and both infinite masses for every 0<epsilon<1. Absolute continuity of the full current and all smooth traces follows from coefficient integrability. Decreasing approximation refers to the potentials U_N; no monotonicity of their currents or smooth masses is asserted. The proof makes no real W2,1, determinant/NPP equality, or novelty claim. Internal references match the granted premises; no new external theorem is invoked. Sequential checks and two independent focused audits found no critical errors or gaps.
